correctness.rationale: The four target covectors w1=(c,0,s), w2=(0,c,s), w3=(c/2,c/2,t), w4=(c/2,c/2,−t) belong to the ℓ_q unit sphere for q=p/(p−1), c∈(0,1), s^q=1−c^q, t^q=1−2^(1−q)c^q; they all satisfy w_x+w_y=c, so their affine rank is two. The inverse ℓ_p duality map takes these to four ℓ_p unit points with oriented determinant −2a²T(1−2^(2−q)), where a=c^(q−1)>0, T=t^(q−1)>0. This is nonzero exactly when p≠2, giving a primal tetrahedron with coplanar dual images. Appending e4,...,e_(k−1) increases the primal affine dimension by k−4 without restoring image rank, for every legal k,n; at p=2 J is the identity. Independently recomputed the 3×3 determinant and dual inverse norms for p=1.35,1.8,2,2.4,4.3, matching exact signs; the nonzero exact factor establishes all real exponents, not those samples.
